sentences: The journal Science is adding an extra round of statistical checks to its peer-review process, editor-in-chief Marcia McNutt announced today.
The policy follows similar efforts from other journals, after widespread concern that basic mistakes in data analysis are contributing to the irreproducibility of many published research findings.
translations: 《科学》杂志主编马西娅·麦克纳特今天宣布，该杂志将在其同行评审过程中增加一轮额外的统计检查。
在人们普遍担心数据分析中的基本错误导致许多已发表研究结果无法重现之后，这一政策效仿了其他期刊的类似做法。

sentences: "Readers must have confidence in the conclusions published in our journal," writes McNutt in an editorial.
Working with the American Statistical Association, the journal has appointed seven experts to a statistics board of reviewing editors (SBoRE).
Manuscripts will be flagged up for additional scrutiny by the journal's internal editors, or by its existing Board of Reviewing Editors or by outside peer reviewers.
The SBoRE panel will then find external statisticians to review these manuscripts.
translations: “读者必须对我们期刊发表的结论有信心，”麦克纳特在一篇社论中写道。
该杂志与美国统计协会合作，任命了七位专家组成统计审稿编辑委员会（SBoRE）。
稿件将被标记出来，由期刊内部编辑、其现有的审稿编辑委员会或外部同行评审员进行额外审查。
随后，SBoRE小组将寻找外部统计学家来审阅这些稿件。

sentences: Asked whether any particular papers had impelled the change, McNutt said: "The creation of the 'statistics board' was motivated by concerns broadly with the application of statistics and data analysis in scientific research and is part of Science's overall drive to increase reproducibility in the research we publish."
translations: 当被问及是否有特定论文促成了这一改变时，麦克纳特表示：“设立‘统计委员会’的动机源于对科学研究中统计和数据分析应用的广泛担忧，也是《科学》杂志为提高我们所发表研究的可重现性而做出的整体努力的一部分。”

sentences: Giovanni Parmigiani, a biostatistician at the Harvard School of Public Health, a member of the SBoRE group, says he expects the board to "play primarily an advisory role."
He agreed to join because he "found the foresight behind the establishment of the SBoRE to be novel, unique and likely to have a lasting impact.
This impact will not only be through the publications in Science itself, but hopefully through a larger group of publishing places that may want to model their approach after Science."
translations: 哈佛大学公共卫生学院的生物统计学家、SBoRE小组成员乔瓦尼·帕尔米贾尼表示，他预计该委员会将“主要发挥咨询作用”。
他同意加入，因为他“发现SBoRE成立背后的远见是新颖、独特的，并且可能产生持久的影响。”
这种影响不仅会通过《科学》杂志本身的出版物体现出来，还有望通过更多可能希望效仿《科学》杂志方法的出版机构来体现。”

sentences: John Ioannidis, a physician who studies research methodology, says that the policy is "a most welcome step forward" and "long overdue".
"Most journals are weak in statistical review, and this damages the quality of what they publish.

I think that, for the majority of scientific papers nowadays, statistical review is more essential than expert review," he says, but he noted that biomedical journals such as Annals of Internal Medicine, the Journal of the American Medical Association and The Lancet pay strong attention to statistical review.
translations: 研究研究方法论的医生约翰·约阿尼迪斯表示，这项政策是“非常受欢迎的进步”且“早该实施”。
“大多数期刊在统计审查方面很薄弱，这损害了它们发表内容的质量。”
他说：“我认为，对于当今大多数科学论文来说，统计审查比专家审查更为重要。”但他指出，像《内科学年鉴》、《美国医学会杂志》和《柳叶刀》这样的生物医学期刊非常重视统计审查。

sentences: Professional scientists are expected to know how to analyse data, but statistical errors are alarmingly common in published research, according to David Vaux, a cell biologist.
Researchers should improve their standards, he wrote in 2012, but journals should also take a tougher line, "engaging reviewers who are statistically literate and editors who can verify the process".

Vaux says that Science's idea to pass some papers to statisticians "has some merit, but a weakness is that it relies on the board of reviewing editors to identify 'the papers that need scrutiny' in the first place".
translations: 细胞生物学家大卫·沃克斯表示，专业科学家理应知道如何分析数据，但在已发表的研究中，统计错误却惊人地普遍。
他在2012年写道，研究人员应该提高他们的标准，但期刊也应该采取更严厉的态度，“聘请懂统计的审稿人和能够核实过程的编辑”。
沃克斯表示，《科学》杂志将一些论文交给统计学家的想法“有一些优点，但一个缺点是它首先依赖于审稿编辑委员会来识别‘需要审查的论文’”。

sentences:
31. It can be learned from Paragraph 1 that____
A. Science intends to simplify its peer-review process.
B. journals are strengthening their statistical checks.
C. few journals are blamed for mistakes in data analysis.
D. lack of data analysis is common in research projects.
translations:
31. 从第一段可以了解到____
A. 《科学》杂志打算简化其同行评审过程。
B. 期刊正在加强其统计检查。
C. 很少有期刊因数据分析错误而受到指责。
D. 研究项目中缺乏数据分析是普遍现象。

sentences:
32. The phrase "flagged up" (Para. 2) is the closest in meaning to____
A. found.
B. revised.
C. marked.
D. stored.
translations:
32. 短语“flagged up”（第二段）在意思上最接近____
A. 发现。
B. 修订。
C. 标记。
D. 存储。

sentences:
33. Giovanni Parmigiani believes that the establishment of the SBoRE may____
A. pose a threat to all its peers.
B. meet with strong opposition.
C. increase Science's circulation.
D. set an example for other journals.
translations:
33. Giovanni Parmigiani认为，SBoRE的建立可能____
A. 对其所有同行构成威胁。
B. 遭遇强烈反对。
C. 增加《科学》杂志的发行量。
D. 为其他期刊树立榜样。

sentences:
34. David Vaux holds that what Science is doing now____
A. adds to researchers' workload.
B. diminishes the role of reviewers.
C. has room for further improvement.
D. is to fail in the foreseeable future.
translations:
34. David Vaux认为，《科学》杂志现在所做的____
A. 增加了研究人员的工作量。
B. 削弱了审稿人的作用。
C. 还有进一步改进的空间。
D. 在可预见的未来将会失败。

sentences:
35. Which of the following is the best title of the text?
A. Science Joins Push to Screen Statistics in Papers
B. Professional Statisticians Deserve More Respect
C. Data Analysis Finds Its Way onto Editors' Desks
D. Statisticians Are Coming Back with Science
translations:
35. 以下哪项是本文的最佳标题？
A. 《科学》加入推动论文统计审查的行列
B. 专业统计学家应获得更多尊重
C. 数据分析进入编辑的办公桌
D. 统计学家随《科学》回归
